museum: Michael C. Carlos Museum, Emory University
possible_additional_holdings: NBC News (5 Aug 2010, 'Mummy madness: Museum exhibits lure crowds') states the museum 'currently displays animal mummies, including a crocodile, a cat and a hawk, and coffins created for a lizard, an ibis, a snake and a shrew' - popular news source only; object may have been a loan or not yet catalogued online.
notes: Official eMuseum searched (crocodile, crocodile mummy, animal mummy, Sobek, Crocodylus, Kom Ombo, hatchling, medium 'animal remains'): only falcon, cat, dog, bird and fish mummies found; no crocodile mummy record online. Many Egyptian animal mummies came with the 1999 Niagara Falls Museum purchase. Needs direct enquiry to museum.

stated_count_source: Official exhibition page 'Egyptian Animal Mummies: Science Explores an Ancient Religion' (23 Mar-1 Jul 2018): 'the Museum's collection of animal mummies ... include a cat, three crocodiles, two ibises, and three falcons' (https://www.samuseum.org/artwork/exhibition/egyptian-animal-mummies-science-explores-an-ancient-religion/)
possible_additional_holdings: Culture in Crisis project page (V&A platform; project director Jessica Powers) states the conservation project covered 'four crocodiles' among ten animal mummies from the permanent collection (https://cultureincrisis.org/projects/animal-mummies-conservation-at-the-san-antonio-museum-of-art) - possibly a 4th crocodile mummy.
inventory_numbers_known: 91.80.110.b,d (from SAMA photo caption reproduced in Wandering Educators, 4 May 2018)
notes: All mummies X-rayed/CT-scanned with UT Health San Antonio Radiology and San Antonio Zoo for the 2018 exhibition (curator Sarah Schellinger). eMuseum (sanantonio.emuseum.com) behind Cloudflare challenge - individual crocodile records could not be read; eMuseum records exist for falcon, ibis and cat mummies (URLs seen in search results). Priority for manual follow-up / image audit.

possible_additional_holdings: AT5604-0 is a box of 50 mummified reptiles 'incl. crocodiles' of which 4 crocodile mummies were exhibited; exact number of crocodiles in the lot not stated. Record suggests origin in old catalogue #s 1563-1565.
image_license: Metadata CC0 (Smithsonian Open Access); image licence not stated in API for these records
notes: Both on display in 'Eternal Life in Ancient Egypt' (2011). si.edu and collections.si.edu web pages return 403 bot verification; NMNH Anthropology search is JS-only.
